findings.rationale: Valid: the old text locked per lineage_id while scanning by branch. Section 3.5 now takes one allocation lock across lookup and creation, with a fixed order (allocation lock, then lineage lock), and a control for concurrent first dispatches.
Valid: a depth-0 repair could not reserve after the round counter hit 2. Section 3.5 now gives depth-0 repair its own reservation kind (lineage only) that opens a new round.

Valid as a claim-scope defect. Rather than change the counted batch, section 3.5 batch mode now states that SUCCESS promotes only the retry text and the per-round cap, not the depth-0 repair path or the lineage budget, which neither P4 nor observe-only P5 measures.

Valid: a driver wall-clock timeout is task behaviour. runner_timeout is removed from infra_fail in section 1; a timeout is a terminal capability_fail row scored on the repo as left, never rerun; P3b controls added for a live loop and a timeout during a G repair.
Valid: section 6 contradicted section 2 on CLAUDE.md. Both now carry the same single exception, the P2 and P3 inventory rows and grouped-list basenames.

Valid: the round classifier was undefined. Section 3.5 now assigns round_id at a non-gate admission (original hand dispatch or depth-0 repair), unchanged by gate-triggered redispatch, and resets round_retries_used only there.

Valid arithmetic: with the old 10 percent of attempts rule only 29 or 30 valid runs were reachable. Section 1 now allows up to 9 infra_fail attempts per arm (10 percent of 90 slots), so three infra losses and 27 valid runs stay reachable.
Valid: three contradictions or self-citations. Section 6 now matches section 2, section 3.9 drops the numeral and points at 3.5, and the parallel-run sentence cites KR3.
Valid: P3b needs the P3 adapter. The section 4 order paragraph now says P3b starts only when P3 is green on the seeded rail.
Valid: nothing unbound a lineage. Section 3.5 adds a closed flag set on accept, on the owner card of step (1), or by explicit reap, and states one lifetime budget per branch until then.

Valid as a disclosure defect. The power note now says the figures are marginal M1 rates, makes no adequacy claim for the full rule, and requires a full-rule power figure in the P4 batch header before the first counted run; no clause changes (coordinator instruction: note only).

Valid: same root as 4. Removing runner_timeout from infra_fail leaves only runner_error and auth_expired, which are independent of model and application behaviour, so replacement cannot select on treatment-correlated hangs.

Valid: the old completion rule demanded open candidates only for 1, 2, 5. P1 complete is now the execution of the preregistered checks with every candidate honestly labelled; any candidate may stay open and no controlled comparison is required.
Valid: same as 1. Closed by the allocation lock and the concurrent-first-dispatch negative control.
Valid: reservation kinds were inconsistent. Section 3.5 now has gate retry (round and lineage) and depth-0 repair (lineage only), and the evaluation order is rewritten to match.

Valid: record shape mixed per-check and aggregate. Section 3.1 now declares one append-only record per gate invocation with nested per-item results and explicit reason, exit_code and signal fields for not_verified.
Valid: duplicate of 5 plus the SKILL.md claim. Section 2 now says no SKILL.md or reference-doc wiring edit occurs in P0 to P6, and section 6 matches.

Valid: the P3 row pointed at a read list. The P3 row now enumerates every editable path (two new lib files, one call site in scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh, test and fixtures, inventory rows) and keeps the ladder files read-only.
Valid hygiene finding. Restated numbers in the reading-order checklist and 3.9 are replaced by section references; section 3.5 and section 1 stay the sole cap and decision-rule statements.
